title: Episode
description: Something that happened, recorded exactly as received. An episode is a claim about an event, not the event: after admission it is authoritative for what was recorded, when, by whom and why it was believed — not for the world.

subject.description: What the episode is about: a matter, entity, or event subject.

matter.description: Matter this episode is linked to. The link itself is a claim with lineage and is supersedeable (issue #1) — never a payload-decided field.

data.description: The payload, recorded as received. Data only: never parsed as an instruction (B-08).

dsorEvidence.description: Present when this episode carries DSoR evidence under contract ssor-dsor/0.1-draft (spec §5).

paramsDigest.description: Canonical digest of action parameters — not raw secrets.

outcome.description: 'uncertain' is first-class: a timeout is never recorded as failure (spec §5.2).

trace.description: Correlation: the trace recorded before the action. Required; absence triggers the 'uncorrelated' flag (B-23).

checks.description: Checks DSoR ran for itself (permissions, limits, approvals, duplicates). Recorded as DSoR's claims; SSoR never re-evaluates them (B-24).

refusal.description: When outcome is 'refused': the limit or approval that refused, per DSoR's attribution.

authority.description: Designated authority for this fact type per the authority map, as of record time.

provenance.description: Required when a model produced the item.

validTime.description: When the event itself occurred, per the source. Late events are placed by valid time (B-16).

flags.description: Admission-set anomaly flags (spec §5.3–§5.4). Never cleared in place: clearing is a new record.
